solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starts off cold? That means it's obsolete

indicators.note: the starts of the two words before 'means' are taken off, losing each opening letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether starting out chilly makes a thing outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' removes C from COLD and T from THAT, leaving OLD and HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn out and no longer fashionable is described with this idiom, a synonym for out of date.

clue.text: Female duck not recorded

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of the letter O
a live broadcast is not recorded beforehand

explanation.surface: A female duck that nobody has filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for any woman, the usual crossword licence for a female.

clue.text: Menacing women doctors welcome endless pain!

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the doctors hold the next piece inside

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for pain is dropped

parts.note: agony is extreme pain

explanation.surface: An exclamation that doctors should greet unending suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Menacing women' reads as an adjective with a noun, but together they are the definition; 'welcome' is the container signal and 'endless' trims the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce, intimidating women are informally called by the name of fire-breathing monsters.

clue.text: A line intended, say, to signify union

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a line meant, since intended means meant

explanation.surface: A line drawn on purpose to show that two things have joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Political or military alliance, a coming together of parties, is a sense of this word.

clue.text: Tries to win love in royal circles

definitions.meaning: to woo someone, seeking their affection
the households and retinues of monarchs

explanation.surface: A suitor angles for affection among the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means woos; the plural noun names the entourages of sovereigns.

clue.text: Iris's old car fails to start

definitions.note: read as 'Iris is', the definition being the flower name

indicators.note: the first letter of the car's name is lost

parts.note: Morris was a British car maker whose models, like the Morris Minor, are now old

explanation.surface: A woman named Iris has an elderly car that will not start.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is used for certain irises, especially the root used in perfumery.

clue.text: Courage required to repeat all this

definitions.meaning: to work out this crossword a second time

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed to go through the whole thing again.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination is a near synonym of courage; split with a hyphen it means work out again.

clue.text: Alcoholics Anonymous propose changing addictive programme?

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A support group for drinkers suggests a twelve-step programme for addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'addictive programme' is a playful description: viewers get hooked on serial dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running television serial keeps fans hooked episode after episode, a playful description.

clue.text: Giant bird with a partial collar

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: partial means only part of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to collar a criminal is to nick, that is, arrest them

explanation.surface: A huge bird wearing only part of a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives for something enormous, after the Titans of myth.

clue.text: Father is Scot's closest English relative

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
taken as written
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A father declares a Scotsman to be English's nearest kin.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Frisian Islands is reckoned the living tongue most akin to English.

clue.text: Tired out after recording "Shame"

indicators.note: after puts the recording first and the scrambled word behind it

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tired performer brands a recording a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired out' looks like a phrase meaning exhausted, but 'out' is the anagram signal acting on 'Tired', and 'after' places the result behind the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace or loss of reputation; both words work as noun or verb.

clue.text: Uncomfortable situation when roses are replaced!

definitions.text: Uncomfortable situation when roses are replaced!

parts.words: Uncomfortable situation when roses are replaced!
parts.note: a comfortable life is a 'bed of roses'; swap the flowers for spikes and it becomes painful

explanation.surface: Someone swaps the flowers in a pleasant phrase and finds discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a painful situation, the opposite of an easy life, from a fakir's spiked board.

clue.text: Spoils toilet training at first

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Potty training at first ruins things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb but is the noun: plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder taken in war or theft, the noun sense of spoils.

clue.text: Bottom needs little time to put on fat

indicators.note: the bottom word needs, and so takes in, the next piece

parts.note: the base is the bottom of something
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cook's tip that a joint's underside should briefly be greased.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks spoon melted fat over meat while it roasts, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Reject Potter's last objective

definitions.meaning: to vote someone out of a club by secret ballot
in snooker, the last ball a player pots is the dark one worth seven

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's final aim is spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a British cue game in which the black ball is potted last; 'Potter' is a snooker player, not Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude from membership, after the dark ballot balls once used to veto candidates.

clue.text: Tube to opening of Camden theatre, perhaps

indicators.note: opening of takes only the first letter of the place name
perhaps signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Directions for taking the Tube to the start of a Camden theatre run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' tempts you toward the London Underground, but it is a medical tube; 'perhaps' signals that the word theatre is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical tube inserted into the body to drain or deliver fluid.

clue.text: Lose water vapour like terrapins at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Turtles swimming in the ocean give off moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants give off moisture through their leaves, the botanical sense of the verb.

clue.text: Hospital patient given wrong test recordings

indicators.note: the patient is given, and so holds, the next piece

parts.note: a case is a patient under treatment

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is subjected to an incorrect test on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a loose container signal: the patient takes the jumbled word inside; 'wrong' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapes in plastic housings were the standard medium for audio recordings.

clue.text: Drink wine for comfort

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Drinking wine as consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: Support and comfort are synonyms for emotional help.

clue.text: Ring made from ironware, naturally

indicators.note: the answer is made from letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A ring forged from iron goods, as you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena, like a boxing or circus ring, is an enclosed area for contests.

clue.text: No pressure with this sweet little pendant

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for pressure is removed

parts.note: a pear drop is a British boiled sweet
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A small charming pendant that relieves pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: A pear drop is a pear-shaped British boiled sweet; drop its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hanging ornament worn on the ear.

clue.text: Leave out container for rubbish

definitions.meaning: a large open bin for builders' waste

explanation.surface: Advice to bypass the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British name for a large open container for building rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is a verb sense; a British dumpster is the noun sense.

clue.text: Small country bands that keep helmets on

definitions.note: read as things that keep helmets on, a plural noun

indicators.note: small means the country's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: China is a country
straps are bands of material

explanation.surface: A small nation's bands that secure helmets.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps fastened under the jaw hold helmets in place.

clue.text: Caught river fish in suitable container

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: River fish caught and put in a fitting holder.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker basket for holding fish, so suitable for the catch.

clue.text: Body of constables, only half in custody!

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, its second half removed

parts.note: possession is a kind of custody or keeping

explanation.surface: Only half the police force is under arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of people summoned to help a sheriff keep the peace.

clue.text: Tripe, smoked sausage or rhubarb

definitions.meaning: an American spelling of bologna sausage
rhubarb is British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A menu of offal, cured meat or a pudding plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense in slang, and also a variant name for bologna sausage.

clue.text: He makes entries with one in the amazing Tardis

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the rearranged letters
amazing suggests confused letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller aboard Doctor Who's wondrous time machine logs his trips.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tardis is the time machine in the British TV series Doctor Who; 'amazing' turns TARDIS into DIARST, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keeping a journal writes daily entries.

clue.text: In Brobdingnag Gulliver was one of them

definitions.text: In Brobdingnag Gulliver was one of them

parts.words: In Brobdingnag Gulliver was one of them
parts.note: in Swift's land of giants, the visiting Gulliver was tiny by comparison

explanation.surface: A remark about Gulliver's status in Swift's land of giants.
explanation.definitionFit: Small folk such as fairies or leprechauns; among Brobdingnag's giants Gulliver was tiny.
